V.rationale: Visa delivered an outstanding Q2 FY2026 with 17% YoY revenue growth (strongest since 2013 ex-pandemic), 20% adjusted EPS growth to $3.31 (beating consensus of $3.10), and raised full-year guidance to low-double-digit to low-teens revenue growth and low-teens EPS growth. The business exhibits excellent fundamental health: 61% operating margins, 52% net margins, 62% ROE, and an asset-light model with no credit risk. Revenue trajectory is accelerating (QoQ +3%, YoY +17.1%) across all segments, with value-added services growing 27% to ~30% of revenue and commercial/money movement solutions up 24%. The $20B buyback authorization and record $7.9B quarterly repurchase signal management confidence. However, the stock at $321 is only ~14% below its 52-week high of $375.51, and while the forward P/E of ~24x is below historical norms, it is not deeply discounted. Regulatory overhang (Credit Card Competition Act) remains a persistent risk, though legislative progress has stalled. Operating cash flow declined 36% YoY in Q2 to $3.01B, which warrants monitoring though YTD FCF of $9B remains strong. The near-term catalyst of the earnings beat and raised guidance has already played out (stock surged 8.3% post-earnings on Apr 29), limiting further re-rating potential in the immediate term.
